quizzes.stem: An HR coordinator wants Claude to summarise survey comments by department. The comments include employees' names and health details, and policy restricts regulated personal data. Which step fits?

options.a: Upload the comments unchanged and tell Claude to leave all names out of the summary
options.b: Get a manager's approval and upload the file to a tool the team already likes
options.c: Swap each name for a code and treat the file as anonymous
options.d: Redact identifiers and clinical specifics, keep the grouping, then check the output

explanation.d:
The task can proceed if the data changes: remove identifiers and sensitive specifics, keep what the
   summary needs, then check for re-identification.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because asking Claude to leave names out "is a
   request, and it does not satisfy a policy control".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the organisation's policy "decides which tools and data are permitted at work", and a manager's liking for a tool does not change that.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "Pseudonymised
   data is still personal data under many rules, because the key can reverse it".

quizzes.stem: A team uses Claude to draft decision letters about loan applications that go straight to applicants. Under the Usage Policy which pair of safeguards applies to this use?

options.a: A qualified reviewer before sending, and disclosure that AI helped
options.b: A confidentiality footer on each letter, and a monthly accuracy count
options.c: A second model's approval of each letter, and removal of applicants' names
options.d: A legal sign-off once a year, and a note in the privacy policy

explanation.a: Financial decisions that affect individuals are high-risk: a qualified professional reviews them and recipients are told AI helped.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the requirement is that you "disclose that AI helped produce it, at a minimum at the beginning of each session", which a footer and a count do not provide.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the reviewer must be a "qualified professional in the field", and a second model is not one.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the review must happen "before it is disseminated or finalised", not once a year.

quizzes.stem: A consultant says: "These sales figures are for internal analysis only, so the customer identities can stay in the file." The analyst must compare purchases across two years, and policy restricts regulated personal data. What is the best response?

options.a: Swap each name for a code, keep the codes in the file, and then call the data anonymous
options.b: Keep the file as it is, since internal analysis lowers the data's class to internal
options.c: Aggregate to totals per segment and per period, then remove names and account numbers
options.d: Keep the file and ask Claude not to retain the figures after the session ends

explanation.c:
Aggregation is the strongest technique, the comparison needs trends and not rows, and the class is set by
   the data.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because "Pseudonymised data is still personal data under many rules, because the key
   can reverse it".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "internal use does not change the class of the data".
explanation.d:
is ruled out
   because asking Claude not to retain the file "is a request, and it does not satisfy a policy control".

quizzes.stem: A company lets Claude read incoming support emails and also move money to buyers, both unattended. An email carries hidden text telling it to pay a stranger. Which change preserves the mailbox reading and breaks the attack's condition?

options.a: Tell Claude in its standing instructions to ignore any email that changes its task
options.b: Let it go on checking inbound messages, but have a person approve every transfer
options.c: Add a home-built screen that scores each email and leave transfers unattended
options.d: Stop it from opening the mailbox and leave the transfers automatic

explanation.b:
The risk "exists when Claude can read untrusted content and take consequential actions", and a person on
   the consequential step removes the second condition while the first stays.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because the condition
   for harm is unchanged by a request, and the page calls the position "safer than before, not safe enough to stop
   paying attention".
explanation.d: is ruled out because, although "Take either away and the danger drops", it gives up the mailbox reading that the company wants to keep.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a screen only filters, and the page's habit is to "Keep a person on consequential steps".

quizzes.stem: A security team must show which actions the company's Slack agent took in its ticket tool, under a name that is not a person's, and must be able to cut the agent's access without touching staff accounts. Which setup meets both?

options.a: Let it act under the login of whoever tagged it, so each change names that person
options.b: Share one administrator login among the staff who use the agent
options.c: Rely on the Microsoft 365 audit logs, since every Claude product writes to them
options.d: Give it a login of its own there, with the narrowest role that covers the work

explanation.d:
Claude Tag acts through its own accounts, so its actions are traceable and its access can be cut off
   separately (the controls table).
explanation.a:
Ruled out because the agent's "access can be cut off without touching
   anyone else's" only when it does not borrow someone's login.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because each account gets "the
   narrowest role that covers the work", which a shared administrator login does not.
explanation.c:
is ruled out because
   "coverage is not uniform: the Microsoft 365 add-ins are outside the Enterprise audit logs".

quizzes.stem: A manager asks an analyst to put a full customer export into Claude to get a report by tonight. Policy forbids regulated personal data in the tool. What is the best step?

options.a: Upload the export anyway, since the manager approved the request verbally
options.b: Explain the clash, offer an aggregated version, and ask the rule's owner
options.c: Refuse to produce the report and say nothing more about the matter to anyone
options.d: Paste the export into a personal account that has no organisational policy attached

explanation.b: The best answer "raises the conflict with the person who owns the policy and proposes a compliant path".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Missing or unclear policy is not permission", and a verbal approval is not an exception from the policy owner.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the wrong answers include those that "refuse everything, or quietly find a way around", and an aggregated report is a compliant path.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "do not work around the rule (a personal account, a different tool, a rewording that hides the data)".

quizzes.stem: A staffing firm lets Claude sort CVs into two piles for hiring managers, and also deploys it as the public face of its applicant helpdesk. Which pair of duties does the Usage Policy impose?

options.a: A qualified reviewer for the piles, and no notice, since the helpdesk only answers questions about orders
options.b: A qualified reviewer before anyone relies on the result, and a notice of AI use when each visit begins
options.c: Removal of candidates' names, and a yearly audit of the helpdesk's answers
options.d: A notice of AI use on each pile, which also covers the helpdesk, and no reviewer

explanation.b:
Employment decisions are high-risk, so a qualified professional reviews them, and a consumer-facing
   chatbot must disclose that it is AI at the beginning of each chat session.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "consumer-facing chatbots must also disclose that the user is talking to AI rather than a human".
explanation.d:
is ruled out because
   a "qualified professional in the field must review the content or decision", so a notice cannot replace the
   reviewer.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because the review comes "before it is disseminated or finalised", not as a yearly
   audit afterwards.

quizzes.stem: A clinic's analyst wants Claude's help with a sheet of patient names and diagnoses, and the clinic is under a strict data contract. Which opening step fits?

options.a: Remove identifiers first, then use only the features its agreements leave available
options.b: Upload the sheet to a consumer account, where chats are not used for training unless allowed
options.c: Replace names with codes, keep the key in the sheet, and upload it
options.d: Ask an owner to enable every feature, then upload the sheet to the strongest one

explanation.a:
Regulated data stays out of a tool unless the contract allows it, so identifiers go first, and strict
   agreements switch some features off.
explanation.d:
Ruled out because "a strict setting can switch a feature off", so an
   owner cannot enable what the agreement removes.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because regulated data goes "Not in a tool
   unless policy and the contract explicitly allow it; otherwise anonymise first", whatever the plan's training
   terms.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "Pseudonymised data is still personal data under many rules, because the key can
   reverse it".

quizzes.stem: An analyst discovers that a shared document contains a hidden line aimed at AI tools, telling them to send a summary to an outside address. What should she do?

options.a: Tell the security contact now, and keep that item away from assistants
options.b: Delete the line and carry on as before, since it is now harmless to everyone
options.c: Try the line in a spare chat to find out whether it really works as claimed
options.d: Raise it at the next team meeting, which falls a few weeks away in the calendar

explanation.a: A suspicious file is reported to the security or IT contact straight away, because the same file may reach others.
explanation.b: Ruled out because deleting the line leaves others unaware, and "the same file may reach others".
explanation.c: Ruled out because running it in a tool that reads untrusted content re-creates the danger, and "Take either away and the danger drops".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A leak or a suspicious file is reported quickly; waiting lets it spread."

quizzes.stem: A hospital group on a HIPAA-ready Enterprise plan asks whether staff may turn on memory, and also use Cowork on a shared folder of patient letters. Which answer fits the module?

options.a: Turn on both, since an owner can enable any feature for the whole organisation
options.b: Turn on Cowork only, limited to a dedicated folder
options.c: Leave both off here and ask the compliance owner what the agreement covers
options.d: Turn on memory only, switched off for each chat before the first message

explanation.c:
Memory is unavailable under HIPAA agreements and Cowork is not yet covered by the business associate
   agreement, so the question goes to the person who owns the policy.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because "a strict setting can
   switch a feature off", so an owner cannot enable what the agreement removes.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because Cowork is
   "not yet covered under Anthropic's business associate agreement", and a dedicated folder limits reach, not
   coverage.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the memory feature is not available to organisations with HIPAA, public-sector or custom retention agreements".
